Corpus v3: Phase 5 Planning and Decomposition Supplement
This fictional supplement extends the v2 benchmark corpus (OV-AR-25 through OV-CS-25) so that query
decomposition, multi-step retrieval, temporal planning and cross-document comparison can be tested against a
corpus large enough for single-query retrieval to fail in measurable ways. It must be ingested alongside v2, not
instead of it.
Design intent: v2 contains almost no region-specific US material, no region-labelled risks, only two time points for
most topics, and one source per topic. v3 adds region-specific strategy and risk documents, a third risk-committee
time point, a newer quarterly update, a pilot review that partly disagrees with management commentary, and a
deliberate set of gaps (no France, Nordics, Japan or Q3 FY2026 data) so that empty-retrieval and partial-evidence
handling can be tested.

OV-US-26 | US Enterprise Expansion Plan FY2026
Document date: 22 May 2026 | Type: Internal strategy plan | Region: United States
1. Objective
The United States is OrionVault's largest customer-location market at 34% of FY2025 revenue, approximately USD
63 million. The plan aims to grow US enterprise revenue faster than the company average by adding direct sales
capacity rather than channel partners. The US motion remains direct-led because enterprise buyers expect a named
account team and a single contractual counterparty.
2. Sales Capacity Plan
Role Start of FY2026 Planned end of FY2026
Enterprise account executives 38 83
Solutions engineers 14 26
Customer success managers (US) 22 34
Newly hired account executives are expected to need two to three quarters to reach full productivity. During the ramp,
compensation and onboarding cost is recognized before the related bookings, which creates a temporary drag on
operating margin.
3. Target Segments
Priority segments are financial services, healthcare technology, and logistics. VaultGuard is the lead product for
financial-services accounts because regulated buyers connect credential control to audit requirements. Orbit Monitor
remains the entry product for logistics accounts, as in the Northstar Logistics case.
4. US Execution Risks
Procurement lumpiness. Enterprise customers can approve a technical deployment in one quarter and defer the
commercial start date into the next, so quarterly bookings can look weak while the pipeline is healthy.
Sales ramp cost. Adding 45 account executives in one fiscal year front-loads cost. If the ramp slips by one quarter,
the plan assumes an operating-margin impact of roughly 0.4 to 0.7 percentage points for the year.
Hyperscaler bundling. US enterprise buyers are the most likely to be offered bundled monitoring and security
functions by large cloud vendors, which creates pricing pressure on renewals.
Security review cycles. US financial-services buyers run lengthy vendor security questionnaires, which extend sales
cycles by an estimated 30 to 45 days compared with non-regulated buyers.
Regulatory note. The US plan does not rely on regional data-isolation commitments, so the incremental
data-residency cost described for Germany and the United Kingdom is not a primary US risk.

Document date: 28 May 2026 | Type: Internal strategy plan | Region: United Kingdom and Germany
1. Objective
Europe is a growth focus built on channel distribution. The United Kingdom represented 15% and Germany 10% of
FY2025 revenue. The plan targets partner-sourced share of new European bookings rising from 12% at the start of
FY2026 to 35% by year end.

Management expects partner-led acquisition to reduce customer-acquisition cost per new logo by 18 to 22%
compared with direct sales, because partners carry pre-sales and implementation effort.
3. Europe Execution Risks
Loss of direct control. Partners own the day-to-day customer relationship. OrionVault receives less product
feedback and has less visibility into renewal risk for partner-led accounts.
Partner discount. Partners receive a margin of up to 25% of first-year subscription value, which offsets part of the
acquisition-cost saving.
Data-residency cost. German and UK regulated customers increasingly require regional data isolation. Under Data
Residency Standard v2.0 the incremental infrastructure and compliance cost can reduce gross margin by 0.6 to 1.0
percentage points for affected accounts unless pricing is adjusted.
In-region support. Qualifying German regulated customers expect support staff located in Germany, which partners
must supply or OrionVault must hire.
Sovereign-cloud competitors. Local providers market data sovereignty as a differentiator in both markets.
Scope note: this plan covers only the United Kingdom and Germany. It contains no plan for France, the Nordics or
other European markets.

OV-RM-25 | Risk Committee Mid-Year Review 2025
Document date: 12 June 2025 | Type: Risk committee review | Position in series: between OV-RM-24 and OV-RM-26
1. Ranking at Mid-Year 2025
The committee ranked credential-security exposure first, platform availability second, customer concentration third,
and international compliance fourth. International compliance moved up from its 2024 position because Data
Residency Standard v1.2 took effect on 01 January 2025 and German commitments were being negotiated.
2. Sentinel Copilot
Sentinel Copilot was added to the watchlist but not ranked. The committee noted that inference cost and
recommendation accuracy would become reportable risks once customer pilots began.
3. Cloud Dependence
The committee still treated cloud concentration mainly as an availability risk. It recorded for the first time that price
and contract terms with infrastructure providers could become a margin issue, and asked management to track it as a
watch item.
4. Customer Concentration
The ten largest accounts were trending from 20% toward 19% of revenue, and the committee described
concentration as improving but still material.
5. Terminology in 2025
The committee continued to use regional processing burden. It introduced the phrase emerging regional isolation
requirement in a single paragraph, which later became regional data-isolation cost in the 2026 update.
Versioning note: this review sits between the 2024 memo and the 2026 update. A temporal plan that retrieves only
2024 and 2026 will miss the intermediate shift.

OV-FIN-25 | FY2025 Operating Margin Bridge
Document date: 06 May 2026 | Type: Finance memo | Period: FY2024 to FY2025
1. Summary
Operating margin rose from 10.4% in FY2024 (USD 16m on USD 154m) to 14.0% in FY2025 (USD 26m on USD
186m), an improvement of about 3.6 percentage points. Gross margin rose from 68.2% to 71.0%, and
operating-expense leverage supplied the remainder.
2. Bridge
Driver Contribution (pp) Comment
Infrastructure efficiency +1.7 Lower unit cost per monitored workload
Workload utilization +0.7 Better packing of container workloads
Multi-module pricing +0.4 Higher pricing on multi-module contracts
Operating-expense leverage +0.8 Sales and administrative cost grew slower than revenue;
R&D; rose as a share of revenue
Total +3.6
Pricing therefore explains a minority of the improvement, which is consistent with the CFO's statement on the
earnings call that the improvement was not primarily a pricing story.
3. Factors That Could Reverse the Improvement
Cloud pricing. Finance estimates that a 5% rise in unit pricing from the main cloud providers would reduce gross
margin by about 0.9 points.
AI inference. Sentinel Copilot inference is not in the FY2025 cost base. Usage-based cost per active seat could
offset infrastructure gains during pilots.
Regional isolation. Duplicated regional environments for regulated customers increase cost and reduce utilization
gains.
R&D growth. R&D rose from USD 35m to USD 43m. Continued growth faster than revenue would erode the
operating-expense leverage.

OV-APAC-26 | India and Singapore Market Note
Document date: 30 June 2026 | Type: Regional market note | Region: India and Singapore
1. India
India contributed 24% of FY2025 revenue and remains the largest engineering base, with Bengaluru and Pune
centres. Customers are price-sensitive, and Orbit Monitor is the dominant product. Domestic data-location
requirements are met within existing public-cloud regions and add little incremental cost.
2. Singapore
Singapore contributed 8% of FY2025 revenue and hosts a sales office. Financial-services customers prefer
VaultGuard and ask for audit evidence, but contracts rarely require dedicated regional environments. Competition
comes mostly from standalone security vendors.
3. Cost Burden Comparison
Neither India nor Singapore is currently among the markets with high incremental data-residency cost. Germany and
the United Kingdom carry the highest burden. The United States, India and Singapore have no regional isolation
commitment in the 2026 standard.
Scope note: no expansion plan for Japan, Australia or other Asia-Pacific markets exists in this corpus.

OV-CP-25 | Competitive Landscape Memo
Document date: 20 November 2025 | Type: Internal strategy memo
1. United States
The largest competitive pressure comes from cloud-platform vendors that bundle monitoring and security into
enterprise agreements. In FY2025 enterprise win rate against bundled offers was 27%, compared with 41% in
mid-market deals.
2. United Kingdom and Germany
Regional managed-service providers and sovereign-cloud vendors compete on data sovereignty. In Germany,
procurement teams weight in-country processing and German-language support heavily. Win rates are higher when a
local partner is involved.
3. Product Positioning
VaultGuard faces standalone secrets-management vendors. Relay Incident faces smaller incident-response
platforms and is mainly sold as an attach product to existing Orbit Monitor accounts.
4. Implication
Management concludes that the unified workflow, rather than any single module, is the differentiator. Competitive risk
is therefore described as pricing pressure in the US and sovereignty positioning in Europe.

OV-PF-26 | Sentinel Copilot Pilot Review
Document date: 09 September 2026 | Type: Internal pilot review | Data as of 31 August 2026 | Feature identifier: SCP-610
1. Pilot Status
As of 31 August 2026, 46 customer pilots were active and 15 had converted to paid add-on contracts. This compares
with 38 active and 11 converted in OV-Q1-26.
2. Effectiveness
Median investigation time fell by 31% for incidents where analysts followed R1 or R2 recommendations. For
credential incidents using recipe IR-17, the R3 recommendation error rate was 4.2%. In 6% of reviewed cases a
plausible but incorrect recommendation lengthened the investigation.
3. Cost
Inference cost per active seat was 35% above plan in June and 19% above plan in August after model-routing
changes. Month-to-month cost variance remained about 40%, so unit economics are not yet predictable.
4. Customer Behaviour
Nine pilot customers disabled automated recommendations while keeping alert summarization. Regulated customers
requested evidence links and review logs before agreeing to broader rollout.
5. Comparison With Earlier Statements
The review notes that the earnings-call goal of predictable economics before broad rollout has not yet been met, and
that the risk committee's human-review requirement for high-impact actions matches the pilot findings.

5. Strategy and Growth Priorities
For FY2026, management identified four priorities: expand VaultGuard adoption, launch Sentinel Copilot, increase
enterprise sales capacity in the United States, and improve gross margins through infrastructure optimization.
The strategy for Sentinel Copilot is to reduce investigation time rather than replace security analysts. The feature is
designed to summarize alerts, surface related events, and recommend investigation steps. Management expects usage
to expand gradually because customers in regulated sectors require stronger explainability and review controls.
Europe is another growth focus. OrionVault plans to deepen channel partnerships in the United Kingdom and Germany.
Management expects channel distribution to reduce customer-acquisition costs, although partner-led sales can reduce
direct control over customer relationships and customer feedback loops.
6. Technology and Operations
The core platform uses containerized services, a managed relational database layer, public-cloud infrastructure, and
customer integrations. The system processes telemetry events, security events, authentication metadata, and incident
records. The core engineering release cadence is weekly; VaultGuard changes undergo stricter release controls.
Major dependencies include public-cloud providers, third-party identity services, external software libraries, and
customer-configured integrations. An outage or pricing change at a major cloud provider could affect availability or
margins in the affected region.

OV-RM-24 | Risk Committee Memo
Document date: 10 November 2024 | Type: Internal risk memo
1. Risk Priorities at the Time
The 2024 risk committee ranked platform availability, credential-security exposure, customer concentration, and
international compliance as the principal enterprise risks.
The committee noted that cloud concentration was primarily an availability issue at that time, while data residency was
mainly viewed as a compliance overhead. Sentinel Copilot was not yet a committee-level risk because it had not entered
customer pilots.
2. Customer Concentration
The ten largest accounts represented approximately 20% of FY2024 revenue. The committee's view was that
concentration was manageable because the largest individual customer was below 5% of revenue and gross revenue
retention remained above 90%.
3. International Data Processing
Germany-specific storage commitments were expected to be the most demanding among the company's then-current
markets. The memo recommended standardized contractual language rather than separate infrastructure environments
for every customer.
4. Risk Language Used in 2024
The committee used the phrase regional processing burden for the cost of keeping data in separate locations. It used
cloud concentration for dependence on external infrastructure providers.
Versioning note: this is deliberately old. Later documents revise both the risk ranking and the technical interpretation of regional
processing.

OV-RM-26 | Risk Committee Update
Document date: 05 August 2026 | Type: Risk committee update
1. Revised Risk Ranking
The 2026 committee now ranks security and trust, data-residency cost, AI recommendation reliability, and cloud
concentration above customer concentration. Customer concentration remains material but is not the fastest-moving risk
in the committee's current view.
2. AI Reliability Risk
Sentinel Copilot introduces a new operational risk because incorrect recommendations can increase investigation time
rather than reduce it. The committee requires production deployments to retain a human review step for high-impact
actions.
3. Data Residency Risk
Germany and the United Kingdom now require stronger regional-storage commitments for a subset of regulated
customers. Management estimates that the incremental infrastructure and compliance cost can reduce gross margin by
0.6 to 1.0 percentage points for affected accounts unless pricing is adjusted.
4. Revised Terminology
The committee now uses regional data-isolation cost rather than the older phrase regional processing burden. It also
distinguishes cloud concentration from cloud provider bargaining exposure, the latter referring to price and
contractual leverage rather than availability.

OV-PR-26 | Sentinel Copilot Product and Technical Brief
Document date: 12 August 2026 | Type: Product brief | Product: Sentinel Copilot
1. Product Definition
Sentinel Copilot is an assistive security-operations feature layered on top of OrionVault's alert and incident data. Its
primary functions are alert summarization, related-event grouping, investigation-step recommendation, and incident
timeline drafting.
Internal product identifier: SCP-610. Credential-incident investigation recipe: IR-17. Recommendation confidence bands
are labeled R1, R2, and R3. R1 recommendations are informational; R3 recommendations require an explicit human
confirmation before execution.
2. Technical Flow
The feature receives normalized alert events, selected identity metadata, recent incident context, and approved runbook
excerpts. A model router chooses a model based on task risk. High-risk recommendations may use a larger model and
stricter verification checks.
Component Role Identifier / policy signal
Alert summarizer Turns a stream of alerts into a concise incident summary SUM-02
Event linker Connects related telemetry and identity events LINK-08
Investigation recommender Suggests next investigative steps IR-17
Timeline builder Drafts a chronological incident record TL-04
High-impact action gate Requires human confirmation for R3 actions HAG-03
3. Cost and Reliability
The primary economic risk is model-inference cost per active seat. The primary reliability risk is recommendation error. A
plausible but incorrect recommendation can be more damaging than an explicit abstention because analysts may spend
time following the wrong path.
4. Supported Integrations
Sentinel Copilot integrates with Relay Incident, VaultGuard, approved identity providers, and selected customer SIEM
exports. Unsupported integrations return the internal status code SCP-UNSUPPORTED-17. Authentication failures in the
Copilot gateway use OV-AUTH-4017. A stale incident context can trigger CTX-2204.
5. Launch Constraints
The product brief requires evidence-linked recommendations, configurable retention, and a human-review workflow for
R3 actions. It does not authorize autonomous credential rotation or production access changes.

OV-IR-21 | Incident Report - VaultGuard Event
Incident date: 18 October 2021 | Type: Security incident retrospective
1. Summary
A VaultGuard configuration defect caused a subset of service-credential metadata to be written with incorrect regional
routing tags. The defect did not expose credential values, but it caused audit records to appear in the wrong regional
partition for 47 enterprise tenants.
2. Timeline
Time Event
09:10 UTC Configuration release 2021.10.18 deployed to a subset of VaultGuard regions.
10:05 UTC First tenant reported an audit-log location mismatch.
10:22 UTC Engineering reproduced the issue under a specific regional-routing configuration.
11:10 UTC Deployment rollback initiated.
13:40 UTC Regional routing tags corrected; validation checks expanded.
18:20 UTC Affected audit records re-indexed into intended regional partitions.
3. Root Cause
The root cause was a configuration mapping defect in a routing component that treated a region alias as globally unique.
The defect passed existing tests because test fixtures covered service availability but did not validate regional audit
placement.
4. Corrective Actions
OrionVault added regional-placement tests, deployment checks for routing-map changes, and a secondary audit-path
verification. The incident led to stricter VaultGuard release controls and became a reference point in later discussions
about regional data isolation.
5. Lessons Relevant to Future RAG
The incident should not be treated as evidence of credential theft. The report explicitly says that credential values were
not exposed. Retrieval systems should distinguish availability, confidentiality, and data-location incidents rather than
collapsing all security events into a generic breach label.

OV-DR-25 | Data Residency Standard v1.2
Effective date: 01 January 2025 | Type: Policy
1. Scope
Version 1.2 applies to customers purchasing regional-storage commitments in Germany and the United Kingdom.
Standard telemetry may be processed in approved multi-region environments unless the contract explicitly requires local
processing.
2. Regional Requirement
For customers with a Germany regional-storage commitment, authentication metadata and incident records must remain
in the approved Germany processing environment. Cross-region replication is permitted for disaster recovery only when
the replicated dataset is encrypted and the customer contract allows it.
3. U.K. Requirement
For designated U.K. customers, customer-configured incident records should remain in U.K. storage. Management
monitoring and anonymized service telemetry may continue to use multi-region infrastructure.
4. Operational Note
The 2025 policy emphasizes contractual configuration and approved processing locations. It does not require all
engineering telemetry to remain in the customer's region.

OV-DR-26 | Data Residency Standard v2.0
Effective date: 01 July 2026 | Type: Policy
1. Scope
Version 2.0 supersedes v1.2 for new and renewed contracts that include regional data-isolation commitments.
2. Germany
For qualifying German regulated customers, identity metadata, security-event records, and incident records must remain
within the designated Germany region. Disaster recovery copies must use an approved Germany-based recovery
boundary unless a contractual exception has been documented.
3. United Kingdom
For qualifying U.K. customers, identity metadata and incident records must remain within the U.K. region. Selected
security telemetry may use approved cross-border processing only when it is pseudonymized and the contract permits it.
4. Engineering Telemetry
Version 2.0 expands the regional requirement beyond customer-visible records. Certain operational telemetry associated
with regulated workloads must be processed within approved regional boundaries. This increases redundancy and
monitoring requirements.
5. Change from v1.2
The major change is the broader definition of regional data isolation. The 2026 standard covers additional security
telemetry and narrows disaster-recovery exceptions for qualifying regulated customers.

Management has identified four priorities for FY2026: expand VaultGuard adoption, launch Sentinel Copilot, increase

7. Key Risks
Cloud infrastructure concentration: The platform depends on third-party cloud infrastructure. A prolonged outage,
pricing change, or regional capacity shortage could affect availability or margins.
Security and trust risk: Because VaultGuard stores customer credentials and security-related configuration, a serious
vulnerability or breach could damage customer trust, increase incident-response costs, and lead to contract losses.
Competition: Larger cloud vendors can bundle monitoring and security capabilities into broader infrastructure
contracts. This may make price-sensitive customers harder to win or retain.
AI cost and reliability risk: Sentinel Copilot may require significant model-inference capacity. Unexpected usage
could increase cost per customer, while inaccurate recommendations could reduce user trust.
Regulatory and data-residency risk: Different regional requirements may require additional controls, audits, and
infrastructure. The burden is particularly relevant in Germany and the United Kingdom.
Customer concentration: The top ten customers account for 19% of revenue. Loss of a major enterprise account
could have a noticeable effect on quarterly results.
Hiring and retention: The company competes for security engineering, distributed-systems, and machine-learning
talent. Wage inflation or attrition in these areas could slow product delivery.

CEO Mira Sen said the company will prioritize durable subscription growth over short-term expansion into low-margin

gross-margin improvement than price increases during FY2026.

cautioned that longer procurement cycles may make quarterly bookings uneven.
